dialogues.speaker: Venier
dialogues.text: So tired... My arm hurts... It's like someone hit it, or something.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Would anyone dare to fight you?

dialogues.speaker: Venier
dialogues.text: Ah, my friend! Where did you learn to judge a book by its cover so?

dialogues.speaker: Venier
dialogues.text: I am a musician, you see! These arms are most elegant when they pluck a lyre's strings, I assure you.

dialogues.speaker: Venier
dialogues.text: Although I do not know why, though I was exhausted after waking up from a lengthy dream, my arms now feel like they have been granted manifold strength.

dialogues.speaker: Venier
dialogues.text: I've never been this tired, not even when I would play the lyre without rest or sleep.

dialogues.speaker: Venier
dialogues.text: It seems that I shall have to return to Capitolium to get some rest...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Venier
dialogues.text: Goodbye. Sorry, but I can't even... wave goodbye to you properly.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's the Capitolium?

dialogues.speaker: Venier
dialogues.text: Capitolium? Why, it's... it's... Wait. Where is it again?

dialogues.speaker: Venier
dialogues.text: Strange. Why did that word suddenly leave my lips? It's as if it was my hometown, where my family is.

dialogues.speaker: Venier
dialogues.text: *sigh* Alas, but I no longer have any family.

dialogues.speaker: Venier
dialogues.text: If this Capitolium is some dream world or the afterlife, may I reunite with them there!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Could you tell me about your family?

dialogues.speaker: Venier
dialogues.text: My daughter inherited my musical gifts, and we were to perform at the Opera Epiclese together.

dialogues.speaker: Venier
dialogues.text: But I... lost her in the dissolved young women case...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sorry for your loss...

dialogues.speaker: Venier
dialogues.text: Grief will not simply disappear. We can only let it slowly fade.

dialogues.speaker: Venier
dialogues.text: I once thought the world unjust for this reason, but will any amount of that change the past?

dialogues.speaker: Venier
dialogues.text: The more I can commit to the Iridescence Tour, the fewer opportunities there will be for sorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Venier
dialogues.text: Perhaps Dvorak, bless his good heart, was just trying to help get me on my feet when he asked for my assistance with the festival!
